title: Compatibility equations for truncation cocone
statement: For the canonical truncation maps j and c into derived cohomology, c is invertible, j satisfies the alpha diagonal cocone equation, and j equals the incoming alpha iterate followed by c for every nonnegative page.

proof.text: Normalize alpha to arbitrary equal total-degree and truncation indices. Substitute hD and hH, expand halpha and hj, cancel bridgeIso.hom with bridgeIso.inv, combine the three functor maps, and use transition_comp_ιTruncLE. eqToHom_naturality of the truncation inclusion supplies the remaining index transport. This proves the diagonal cocone equation.

Regard Q(tau_{<=n}K) and Q(K) as bounded-below derived objects. The truncation inclusion is a cohomology isomorphism for i<=n by CochainComplex.quasiIsoAt_ιTruncLE and homologyFunctorFactors naturality; its source has zero homology at n+1, so that degree map is monic. Apply isIso_homologyFunctor_rightDerivedFunctorPlus_map. Naturality of rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility.inv transports the degree-n isomorphism to the unbounded right derived functor. Then hc and hj express c as this map composed with bridge and object isomorphisms.

Set k(n,p)=eqToHom followed by j(n,n-p). The cocone equation is alphaDiagonal(n,p) followed by k(n,p)=k(n,p+1). Induct on r to show alphaIter(r,p,q) followed by the transported k(n,p-r) equals the transported k(n,p) whenever p+q=n. The base is the identity; the successor uses the induction hypothesis at (p-1,q+1) and the cocone equation at p-1. Specialize p to a nonnegative integer cast from Nat and use hc at the endpoint to obtain the incomingAlphaIter identity.

theorem truncation_abutment_cocone_aux
    {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} A] [Abelian A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v₁} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} A]
    {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} B] [Abelian B]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v₂} B] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} B]
    (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F]
    (K : CochainComplex.Plus A) (X : BigradedExactCouple B 0)
    (hD : X.D = TruncationCouple.D F K)
    (halpha : ∀ p q : ℤ, X.alpha p q =
      eqToHom (by rw [hD]) ≫ TruncationCouple.alpha F K p q ≫
        eqToHom (by rw [hD]))
    (H : ℤ → B) (hH : H = fun n : ℤ ↦ (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B n).obj
      (F.rightDerivedFunctor.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K.obj)))
    (j : ∀ n q : ℤ, X.D (n - q) q ⟶ H n)
    (c : ∀ n : ℤ, X.D 0 n ⟶ H n)
    (hj : ∀ n q, j n q = eqToHom (by rw [hD]; unfold TruncationCouple.D; congr 1; omega) ≫
      (TruncationCouple.bridgeIso F (TruncationCouple.truncation K q) n).inv ≫
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B n).map
        (F.rightDerivedFunctor.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map (K.obj.ιTruncLE q))) ≫
      eqToHom (by rw [hH]))
    (hc : ∀ n, c n = eqToHom (by congr 1; omega) ≫ j n n) :
    (∀ n, IsIso (c n)) ∧
    (∀ n p, X.alphaDiagonal n p ≫ eqToHom (by congr 1; omega) ≫ j n (n-p) =
      eqToHom (by congr 1; omega) ≫ j n (n-(p+1))) ∧
    (∀ (n p : ℤ) (_ : 0 ≤ p), eqToHom (by congr 1 <;> omega) ≫ j n (n-p) =
      X.incomingAlphaIter p.toNat 0 n ≫ c n)
